question.problem:
A smartphone app monitors the number of new subscribers, $S(t)$, in thousands, each day since its launch. The following table shows the rate at which new subscriptions are arriving.

| **$t\,\text{(days)}$** | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${S}^{′}(t)\,\text{(thousands/day)}$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ | $2$ | $5.5$ |

$$

$$

At the time $t=6,$ the app had $4$ thousand subscribers. Use the tangent line approximation of $S$ at time $t=6$ to approximate the number of subscriptions at $t=7.$

current_example.problem: Suppose that $f(-2) = 0$ and $f'(-2)=2.$ Estimate the value of $f(-1.8)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=-2.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $f(x)$ at the point $a=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2)(x-(-2)) \\  & =0+2(x+2) \\  & =2(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-1.8)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=-1.8.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1.8) & ≈L(-1.8) \\  & =2(-1.8+2) \\  & =2(0.2) \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$
